title: GPU canvas: very large documents run the GPU out of memory, then the CPU fallback reads every pixel (300000² hangs the app)
review_rationale: The reported GPU-to-whole-document-CPU fallback is not Varve’s architecture: Canvas2D is the authoritative renderer, and WebGPU admits only simple solid shapes. The transferable low-zoom cost is real for Varve paint layers: the accepted ADR-0214 pyramid remains unimplemented, while the 2026-08-09 baseline exceeds a 16.7 ms frame at 2048² and measures a 256 MiB intermediate at 8192². Photo fills also remain a separate full-decode/viewport gap. Varve’s Transform Pixels path is explicitly bounded (maximum 16,777,216 selected-operation pixels, with target/source/output planes limited to about 5.6 MP) but its resampling and PNG commit are synchronous; no slow user interaction at the admitted limit has been reproduced, so that remains a profiling lead rather than a confirmed defect. The marketing site makes no large-document performance claim to change.

varve_review.rationale: PhotoCraft #1015 documents measured GPU budget failures, whole-document CPU redraws and multi-second transform commits. Varve avoids the same GPU failure shape through Canvas2D authority and bounded transform selection, while the independently measured raster-layer LOD gap remains applicable.
varve_review.source_scope_note: Read the issue body and all 10 comments, including sample document details, measured 60k²/300k² fallback behavior, the actual 6.4 GB PSB workflow, and the later distinct Free Transform and Warp stalls. Reviewed merged PR #1427 (notice after a completed slow fallback), merged #4218 (background transform job with progress/cancel), and open #5590 (background Warp job); #6800 is performance optimization evidence and does not remove the UI-thread concern. Compared these with Varve’s renderer, accepted raster-pyramid decision and baseline, image lifecycle gaps, and bounded Transform Pixels implementation. Photo fills and paint-raster layers are distinct code paths; no external sample is imported or benchmarked in Varve. No marketing claim change is justified.

marketing_review.evidence: apps/website source reviewed: no large-document or GPU-fallback performance promise found

validation.command: source and architecture comparison; no implementation in this disposition
validation.result: partial match documented; raster LOD remains an existing measured project gap

title: fix(format): a document holding a NaN or infinite float saves to a .pcraft that cannot be reopened
engineering_status: DocumentCodec.encode normalizes non-finite adjustment parameters; round-trip regression passes
review_notes: Commenter supplied a failing engine round-trip test for serializing NaN as JSON null; reverse direction from F-001, not assumed same root cause.
review_rationale: The report supplies a non-finite adjustment value that JSON serialization turns into null, making a saved document unreadable in PhotoCraft. Varve already normalizes adjustment parameters before DocumentCodec.encode serializes them; a new encode/decode regression verifies a NaN exposure value is repaired to the finite default and the document reopens. This is covered behavior rather than a newly reproduced Varve defect.

varve_review.rationale: DocumentCodec.encode runs adjustment normalization before JSON serialization, which removes the invalid non-finite parameter that would otherwise become JSON null. The new test checks the exact save/decode round trip from the report.
varve_review.source_scope_note: Read issue body and sole comment containing a Session save/load reproduction. Varve unit test passes for a NaN exposure parameter via DocumentCodec.encode and decode. This covers the reported adjustment payload class; it does not claim that arbitrary non-finite values in every scene field are sanitized on save.

title: Crop tool: a pending crop leaks into other documents (New, Open, switching tabs)
review_rationale: Varve reproduces the shared-session risk at source level: CropTool stores pending state on a singleton ToolManager, while active tabs can change. The session synchronization hook now exits Crop mode on active session/document change. A real Chromium workflow imported an image, changed a pending crop, created a new document tab, and verified the overlay was absent and Enter left the new tab active. The matching PhotoCraft failure was fixed upstream in PR #1957 by associating pending state with its document and cancelling stale state before draw/commit. Varve uses the simpler cancel-on-session-change policy; Krita's manual describes recalling a previous crop but leaves cross-image reuse unspecified.

varve_review.rationale: Varve reproduces the shared-session risk at source level: CropTool stores pending state on a singleton ToolManager, while active tabs can change. The session synchronization hook now exits Crop mode on active session/document change. A real Chromium workflow imported an image, changed a pending crop, created a new document tab, and verified the overlay was absent and Enter left the new tab active. The matching PhotoCraft failure was fixed upstream in PR #1957 by associating pending state with its document and cancelling stale state before draw/commit. Varve uses the simpler cancel-on-session-change policy; Krita's manual describes recalling a previous crop but leaves cross-image reuse unspecified.
varve_review.source_scope_note: Read the issue and all three comments, including the maintainer reproduction and Photoshop behavior check; read the merged linked PR discussion and its cancellation-before-draw/commit strategy; checked Krita’s official crop manual; it leaves cross-image reuse unspecified. In Varve, the complete crop pointer spec passed in Chromium (14/14), including the new-tab path, cancel, commit, undo and redo cases. The screenshot was inspected at 1280x721. File-open and direct tab-switch routes share the same active-session synchronization code but were not separately pointer-driven in this run.

title: [High][Data loss] Flatten All Layer Effects deletes layer and vector masks, including disabled masks
engineering_status: adjacent design lead; Varve has no command that bakes live effects while preserving masks, so this report does not establish a defect in an equivalent operation.

This is useful as a design constraint if a selective effect-bake command is added, but no existing Varve operation with the reported contract is shown defective.

title: layer.vectorMask.edit accepts any feather, and 1e39 is stored as infinity so the document can't be saved
review_rationale: PhotoCraft PR #4202 confirms a finite 0..=1000 px contract. Varve previously preserved non-finite edits and left finite radii unbounded, allowing excessive blur initialization work. The committed fix bounds setter, add, load validation, and Inspector input. Eighty scene/codec tests pass; dark, light, and high-contrast Inspector visuals and save/reopen at the 1000 px cap were checked. The Inspector unit file is present but its focused test has not yet completed. No website claim needs revision.

varve_review.rationale: PhotoCraft PR #4202 confirms a finite 0..=1000 px contract. Varve previously preserved non-finite edits and left finite radii unbounded, allowing excessive blur initialization work. The committed fix bounds setter, add, load validation, and Inspector input. Eighty scene/codec tests pass; dark, light, and high-contrast Inspector visuals and save/reopen at the 1000 px cap were checked. The Inspector unit file is present but its focused test has not yet completed. No website claim needs revision.
varve_review.source_scope_note: Compared the complete #4201 report and merged #4202 discussion with Varve mask setter, document validation, blur initialization, and Inspector action. The upper-bound Inspector clamp was added after a browser save/reopen attempt exposed a document that the loader rejected. Dark/light/high-contrast views and save/reopen at 1000 were visually checked. Eighty scene/codec tests pass; focused Inspector unit remains pending. Website claim scan found no relevant copy.

title: Gradient/Pattern Fill layers accept angle 1e39 or phase 1e39, and the document can no longer be saved
engineering_status: No same f32 overflow found in Varve document fields, which use f64; comparable angle normalization and pattern bounds are not established as a Varve defect. Linked PRs #5753 and #5831 contain competing fixes and an incomplete malformed-phase case.
review_notes: Issue and both comments read; #5753 and #5831 body, commits, and review discussion inspected. Both open at cutoff B. #5753 has an approval and review notes that a non-array pattern phase is silently ignored; its reviewer flags #5831 as duplicate. #5831 review advises choosing one or rebasing and notes malformed values now error. Varve numeric document fields use f64, so the f32 overflow/save failure is not directly applicable.
review_rationale: The reported 1e39 gradient/pattern values overflow PhotoCraft f32 fields, but Varve stores scene/bridge numbers as f64; no matching save corruption is established. Angle normalization may be a product consistency choice, and the issue reports no incorrect render at the unchanged 450-degree angle. Keep as an analogue, not a confirmed Varve defect.

review_notes: Body describes recursive compound-shape failure for Affinity Photo import; Varve does not support .afphoto import. Verify links and disposition before closing.
review_rationale: The reported Affinity compound importer is not supported in Varve. Cross-app evidence prompted comparison with Varve’s supported PSD/PSB importer, where both recursive converters lacked tree limits. An iterative preflight now rejects nesting over 64, more than 50,000 nodes, more than 500,000 child slots, and repeated references before conversion. The @webtoon/psd dependency still recursively freezes groups before returning a tree; that earlier failure remains caught at the import boundary and documented.

varve_review.rationale: Varve has no Affinity importer. PSD/PSB group conversion is supported and had an analogous recursive-work gap; bounded preflight now rejects malformed or oversized returned trees before scene conversion. The upstream dependency’s pre-return recursive freeze remains a documented limitation.

title: Layer styles, solid color fill, channels, artboards, count groups and type.create store 1e39 as infinity; the document can no longer be saved
review_notes: overflow symptom across commands; bot suggests #5752/#4201/#4181; recursive links remain under review.
review_rationale: The reported persisted-document corruption is not a direct Varve match because the document and native bridge retain f64 values. Review reproduced an adjacent defect in the opt-in native GPU render planner: finite f64 shape/path coordinates could narrow to f32 infinity and still form a presentable plan. Committed admission checks reject that frame before device submission and retain Canvas2D fallback. Accelerator tests and Clippy pass; the dependent desktop Rust lane remains unverified because shared disk capacity fell below 100 MB during Tauri compilation.

varve_review.rationale: The exact PhotoCraft save-failure mechanism does not apply to Varve persistence, but its f32-overflow report exposed an adjacent native GPU admission defect. Shape records and transformed path/cover vertices are checked after narrowing, with partial paths rolled back so incomplete plans take the authoritative fallback. The implementation is committed; accelerator tests, Clippy, docs and emoji audits pass. Dependent desktop tests could not complete under shared disk pressure.
varve_review.reviewer_engineering_status: Adjacent opt-in native GPU overflow reproduced and fixed; incomplete plans fall back; dependent desktop Rust tests pending due disk capacity.
varve_review.source_scope_note: Reviewed the complete issue and linked numeric-overflow reports, compared Varve scene/bridge types and native GPU lowering, and added regressions for finite 1e39 shape and path coordinates. The renderer declines invalid plans before GPU submission. No marketing claim applies. Desktop integration remains unverified because the shared filesystem could not safely support a full Tauri test build.

title: .pcraft: a number beyond the f32 range opens as infinity, and the document can then never be saved
engineering_status: No matching Varve f32-narrowing failure established. Varve stores document numbers as JS/Rust f64; its separate decode guard rejects JSON values that become non-finite in JS (for example 1e309).
review_notes: Issue and two comments reviewed; PR #6863 body/timeline reviewed. PhotoCraft reproduces a finite f64 value (1e39) narrowing to f32 infinity; Varve document and bridge models use f64, so this exact save failure is not established. Varve separately rejects JSON values that parse as non-finite JS numbers.
review_rationale: The reported value 1e39 is finite in JavaScript and is stored as f64 in Varve document/bridge models; the PhotoCraft failure requires f32 narrowing and does not transfer directly. Varve has an analogous but distinct guard for JSON values that parse as non-finite in JS, such as 1e309. Retain as an analogue and keep the independent Varve decode-boundary fix tracked under F-001.
